Type designates different kinds of body decorations. Often this FE will label part of a multi-word or compound word target.

This frame covers descriptions of an entire human body, viewed as a gestalt (as opposed to descriptions based on salient body parts). The Frame Elements are Individual and Figure. Chuck is muscular. Chuck has a muscular body.
This FE identifies the Degree to which a body has a particular characteristic.
This FE identifies the individual (or individuals) being described.
This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target.
This frame is concerned with words that describe a person based on a salient part of their body. He was a blonde guy. He was a peg-leg.
This FE identifies theIndividual (or individuals) being described.
This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target.
This FE identifies the Degree to which the body description applies.

In this frame a Body_mark is present on a Possessor's body. It may be located at an Attachment and have a Descriptor. A Cause may also be indicated. It may be a temporary condition or a permanent one. Mark has a cancerous mole on his back.
The Attachment is the larger body part to which the Body_mark is attached, or of which it is a part.
This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Body_mark. it identifies a modifier of its head noun.
This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Body_mark.
The Cause is the event that brings about the presence of the Body_mark.
A specific kind of the particular Body_mark.
Salient constituents that make up the Body_mark.

This frame contains words for motions or actions an Agent performs using some part of his/her body. A number of words in this frame occur as blends with Communication, in which the action has an Addressee. For example, Pat nodded at Kim. These examples differ from Communication.Gesture in that no specific message need be expressed, as in She nodded to him to sit down. Since this frame involves a particular type of motion, it contains the frame elements Source, Path, Goal and Area, which originate in the motion frame. All of these frame elements are generally expressed in PP Complements. The boy swung his legs from under the table.
The Agent uses some part of his/her body to perform the action. Agent occurs as the External Argument.
With some verbs in this frame, the Body_part involved in the action is specified by the meaning of the verb and cannot be expressed separately. For example,
Body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement.
Cause is something in the external environment that causes the Agent to move part of his/her body. Cause is usually expressed in a PP Complement:.
Addressee only occurs in the Body-movement frame in sentences which are blends with Communication. Where it occurs, it is typically a PP Complement:
Source is the place from which the Body_part is moved.
Path identifies the trajectory of motion of the Body_part without specifying a start or end point.
Goal is any expression that identifies the endpoint of movement.

Area identifies any expression describing a region in which the motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. (This FE should be contrasted with Place.)
This FE identifies the Degree to which the event occurs.
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the body movement occurs.
This FE identifies the Result of an event.
This FE identifies the Message that the body movement conveys.
This FE identifies the Time when the body movement occurs.
This FE specifies the subregion of the body that is involved with movement.
The purpose of the body movement.
This FE identifies the event noun of the verb.
The period of time during which the movement of a Body_part occurs.
The location within which the movement of a Body_part takes place.
An alternative description of the Body_movement.
An event that the Agent perceives and responds to by moving in coordination with it.

A Financial_instrument (a bond or insurance) fulfills a condition at a certain Time after which the Issuer of the Financial_instrument is legally obligated to pay the Holder a monetary Value, based on the instrument's original Principle and the Interest rate. The bond had matured to its full value at 30 years.
The bond, insurance, or debt security which a Holder buys from an Issuer.
The entity which is obligated to pay the Holder after the Financial_instrument matures.
The entity which owns the Financial_instrument and is owed money from the Issuer.
What the Financial_instrument is worth after maturity.
The amount that the Holder originally paid to own the Financial_instrument.
The growth rate on the Principle that results in the final Value of the Financial_instrument.
This frame contains words that describe a Boundary between two Entities. In many cases, the Boundary is the border between an Entity and some unnamed space, generally conceived of as empty.
The region which is between the Entities or between the Entity and empty space.
The entity that has a Boundary.
The joint construal of both Entities next to the Boundary.
The relative location of the boundary in respect to the Entity or Entities.
This is an abstract frame for bounded areas, used mostly for FE inheritance.
This FE identifies a stable Bounded_area. It typically serves as the denotation of nouns.
This FE identifies the salient Constituent_parts that make up a bounded area.
Relative_location identifies the place in respect to which a bounded area is located.
This FE is used for the Name of a bounded area.
This FE identifies theOwner, generally a person, of the bounded area.
This FE identifies the Formational_cause (action or agent) that brings about the features of the bounded area.
An indication of which kind of Bounded_area the entity is.

An Exterior, Surface, Boundary, and Interior are picked out relative to the Ground. This Ground may either occupy only the Boundary (in which case the Interior is negative space) or the Ground may fill the Interior.
A region of space located inside a Ground.
An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Interior, Surface, Boundary, or Exterior regions.
The region located outside of, but in contact with, the Ground.
The region associated with the boundary of the Ground.
The region which is not located inside or in contact with the Ground.

A Speaker talks about a Topic, which may be an action performed by the Speaker or an entity or state of affairs that they are associated with in order to suggest that the Speaker is worthy of admiration. The Speaker may give an explicit Reason why the Topic redounds to their credit. Alternatively, a Message frame element can be used to directly describe what the Speaker says, leaving the more specific Reason for admirability to be inferred. Instead of the Speaker, the action may be attributed metonymically to the Medium, or possibly the Expressor. Turkish officials boasted of giving 'tens of thousands of dollars in surreptitious payments' to a prominent American politician. He then vaunted his own clan, but failed to mention Emanuel Ungaro, who described the omission as ''lamentable''. The press release boasts that "a direct connection between the cartridge and the system" means no more having to blow dust out of game cartridges. 70's comics like Chevy Chase and Steve Martin over-stated their egotism and preened over their superiority.
The Speaker is the person who produces a message about a Topic.
The Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker communicated a message.
The Topic is a positively judged entity or state of affairs with which the Speaker is associated and about which they talk.

Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).
An act whereby the Speaker makes a boastful statement.
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement.
The state of the Speaker during the statement.
The time when the statement is made.
The FE specifies the place where the statement takes place.
A characteristic of the entity or state of affairs denoted by the Topic which explains why the Speaker is proud of the association with the Topic referent.
A description of the state of affairs that redounds to the Speaker's credit
Role is used for the capacity in which the Topic entity or state of affairs is judged, and is expressed in as-PPs.
Expressor is the body part or action that conveys the feeling of pride of the Speaker.
The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Statement event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their speaking.

A Whole breaks apart into Pieces, resulting in the loss of the Whole (and in most cases, no piece that has a separate function). The plane violently broke apart in mid-air. And then, I finally realized that it must have been the case that a meteorite broke apart into at least 3 large pieces.
The Whole goes into Pieces which were not (necessarily) definable subparts prior to breaking.
The Pieces result from the breaking apart of the Whole.
This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.
Any description of the event or participants not covered by more specific Frame Elements.
The time at which the breaking apart takes place.w
The location at which the breaking apart takes place.
An action, event, or state that enables the event of breaking apart.
An single Sub_part breaks off from a Whole. The original sword may have chipped off of the statue long ago.
The part of the Whole that is conceived as being broken or taken off from the remaining part of the whole.
The piece that is presented in a less prominent position, and which is the landmark or remaining whole from which Sub_part breaks off.
This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.
The time at which the breaking off of the Sub_part happens.
The location at which the breaking off occurs.
Any description of the event or participants not covered by more specific Frame Elements.
An action, event, or state that enables the event of breaking off.
An Agent causes Air to move in a direction, usually specifying either in or out of the body.
The Agent's breathing causes the motion of the Air. Agent is generally the External Argument.
Air is the substance that the Agent causes to move.
This FE identifies the point at which theAir ends up as a result of the motion.
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent breathes.
This FE identifies the Means of breathing.
Source identifies the starting point of the Air.
This FE identifies thePath of the motion through locations after leaving the Source and before reaching the Goal.
This FE identifies the degree to which an Agent is breathing.
Depictive identifies a phrase describing a participant in a breathing event.
This FE identifies the Place where the breathing occurs.
This FE idenitfies the Duration of time that an Agent breathes.
The distance that the Air travels.
An entity that allows the Agent to breathe, either a natural part (the lungs, say) or a device (like a respirator).
The time at which breathing occurs.

This FE designates internal events/states that cause the Agent to exhibit the specified type of breathing. Further, the internal state of the Agent is perceivable to others because of the breathing event.
This FE denotes an event or state external to the Agent that causes them exhibit the specified manner of breathing but not as a conscious response to the External_cause.
Circumstances are expressions indicating prevailing physical conditions or states of affairs concurrent to the breathing event.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by breathing in the specified manner.

This frame concerns the movement of a Theme and an Agent and/or Carrier. The Agent, a person or other sentient entity, controls the shared Path by moving the Theme during the motion. In other words, the Agent has overall motion in directing the motion of the Theme. The Carrier may be a separate entity, or it may be the Agent's body. The Constant_location may be a subregion of the Agent's body or (a subregion of) a vehicle that the Agent uses. Karl carried the books across campus to the library on his head. Karl carried the books across campus to the library in his truck. Karl carried the books across campus to the library by truck. The truck carried the books across campus to the library in specially designed boxes. The FEs include Path, Goal, and Source. Area is an area that contains the motion when the path is understood as irregular. This frame emphasizes the path of movement as opposed to the FEs Source or Goal as in Filling or Placing.
The Agent is a sentient being who physically controls the movement of the Theme via the carrier, accompanying the Theme.
Goal identifies the endpoint of the path.
Source indicates the beginning of the path along which the Theme travels.
The Constant_location expresses the location of the Theme relative to the Carrier. This relationship holds for the entire length of the carrying event.
Area is used for descriprion of a general area in which the carrying action takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.
Depictive identifies a phrase describing the Carrier, Agent or Theme.
This FE identifies the Distance the Theme is carried.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Carrier or Agentcarries the Theme.
The Speed is the rate at which the carrying or transporting occurs.
The Purpose for which the Carrier or Agentcarries the Theme.
The Carrier provides support for the Theme. Movement of the Carrier results in movement of the Theme.
The actions the Agent takes to move the Theme.
The Place is the general area that serves as a setting for the specific motion of the Agent and Theme (with Source, Path, or Goal).
The time in which the carrying event takes place.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
This FE describes the particpant for whom the bringing is beneficial.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
This frame element is used to indicate the location of a participant in cases where the multiple participants of an event are not co-located in the typical fashion.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co_participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative.

This frame describes assembly or construction actions, where an Agent joins Components together to form a Created_entity, which is profiled, and hence the object of the verb. Jack built a new house out of bricks. We glued the airplanes together.
This FE identifies the Instrument(s) with which an Agent builds a Created_entity.
This FE identifies the Place where the building occurs.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
This FE identifies the Time when the building occurs.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent builds a Created_entity.
This FE identifies the Components that form the Created_entity.
Created_entity identifies the entity that is created in the act of building.
This FE identifies theResult of the act of building.
Depictive identifes the phrase describing the participant in the act of building.
This FE idenitifies the Manner in which an Agent builds a Created_entity.

This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
This frame includes words that name subparts of buildings that can be occupied by people. Mary left the room in a huff.
This FE is present purely for technical, software reasons.
The entirety of a building whose parts are discussed.

This frame contains words which name permanent fixed structures forming an enclosure and providing protection from the elements. The baroque church, built in 1635, has a very rich interior The city tour includes the 16th-century monastery of the Transfiguration and Church of Elijah the Prophet An ancient stone church stands amid the fields Jack built his house in the style of the day.
The Individual that created the Building.
The entity built by the Builder which has some Function.
The use for which the Building is intended.
The Name used to refer to the Building.
Any indication of what makes up the Building, including components, ingredients, etc
The time at which the Building comes into existence.
An indication of the subtype of Building, including architectural style.
A characterization of some property of the Building.
A place that a Building is located with respect to.
An Agent performs an Action incorrectly. The affected Patient may be mentioned metonymically for the Action. Mickey botched that swing. Julia bungled the cake.
This FE identifies the Degree to which a bungling event occurs.
Depictive identifes a phrase describing a particpant in an action.
This FE identifies the Manner in which theAgent bungles.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent bungles.
The Agent performs an action incorrectly.
Patient is the entity affected by the Agent's bungling of an Action.
This FE identifies the Place where the bungling occurs.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent bungles.
This FE identifies the Time when the bungling occurs.
This FE identifies the Action that the Agent performs incorrectly.
The type of action that the Agent habitually bungles.
A Proprietor owns or runs a Business which provides a Product (which may be goods or services).
Product identifies the product or service provided by the business.
Proprietor is the owner or chief participant in the business.
Descriptor indicates other characteristics of the business besides its Product and Proprietor.
This FE identifies the Place in which the business is located.
Business identifies the company or establishment. This may be the target itself or the Business_Name if it is an appositive not set off with commas (i.e. restrictive):
The name of the Business when it appears in an appositive set off by commas (non-restrictive):
When a Business is described in terms of the professionals who work to produce the product or service, use Service_provider.

Words in this frame name the different parts of the calendric cycle, both man-made and natural. Frame elements include Whole for the whole of which the target is a part, Relative_time (RelT) for locating the time with respect to an identifiable reference point, and Name for the name of the day (month, etc.) of a specially named unit. Words in this frame figure into a variety of temporal schemas, realized as constructions. There are families of constructions in which these words occur, including ones in which weekday names combine with day part names using particular prepositions (e.g. on Wednesday morning, cf. on Wednesday, but in the morning) and ones in which calendric terms fill the slots in multi-word expressions such as N-after-N (e.g. day after day), N-by-N (e.g. week by week), N-to-N (e.g. month to month), etc. More can be found on these in Fillmore (2002). Note, also, the connection between this frame and Iteration, specifically that many iterative adjectives and adverbs are based on calendric terms (e.g. daily, weekly, monthly, etc.).
Relative_time is used for the word or words that locate the time with respect to an identifiable reference point.
Name is used for the name of a day (month, etc.). Note that only the word (or words) that is the name is (are) tagged, not the target word.
Whole is used for the larger unit of which the target word names a part.
The number of intervals of the specified type.
The calendric unit that is denoted. LUs in this frame all denote the Unit.
An event saliently associated with a particular calendric unit.

This frame contains adjectives and nouns that describe the truth or sincerity of communication. These words, analogously to behaver-evaluating words, can apply either to Speakers or to the Messages they produce. They can occur with about-PPs expressing Topic. Evelyn was candid with me about the party.

The Speaker produces the Message, the truth or sincerity of which is at issue. It is normally expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of the target word, or as the Nominal Head of prenominal uses.
The Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated. This FE often remains unexpressed. When expressed, it normally takes the form of a PP Complement headed by with.

Message is the communicative content whose truth or sincerity is at issue. This FE does not normally co-occur with the other FEs in this frame. When it does occur, it is normally the External Argument of a predicative use of the Target word, or the modified Nominal Head in a prenominal use.

The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It often occurs without the Message FE in predicative uses of the target word. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about".
Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.
This FE identifies the Degree to which a communication is candid--some are more candid than others.
This FE indicates the manner of candidness.

An Entity meets the pre-conditions for participating in an Event. A Degree modifier may be included to indicate by how much the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements. Conductor software gives us the hands-on capability to provide updates immediately The GOP is afraid that it might not be able to keep the seat vacated by Dunn. NASA is unable to communicate with Mars rover. He can fly a kite.
The Entity whose meeting or falling short of pre-conditions is assessed.
The Event that the Entity may participate in.
The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Event.
The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions.
An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to be meet or fail to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Event.
The characteristic or behavior of the Entity that is considered when judging whether the Entity might participate in the Event.
The particular role that the Entity plays in the Event.
An Entity has the ability to contain a Theme. Our facility seats up to 500 people.
The Entity whose ability to contain items is assessed.
The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for holding the items.
The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions for containing.
An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to be able or unable to hold the items.
The status of the capability (e.g., innately, with modifications).
The Entity has the ability to contain the Theme, often expressed with a quantity.
A description of one of the participants, typically theTheme but possibly the Entity.
This FE denotes a sub-part of the Entity which has a particular capacity.
The Purpose of the Entity's specified capacity.
The Time at which the Entity has or had a certain capacity.

This is the primary frame evoked by the cardinal numbers. Dr. Malik has confined almost a score of such unfortunates in his basement, you know. There were thirty of the little blue creatures staring up at him. Stephen has more than five hundred in his closet! DNI There are just over six billion people in the world today.
This FE identifies the Entity enumerated by the Number.
This FE identifies the Precision to which an Entity approximates a Number.
How many times larger the group of Entitys is than the base Number.

A Distributor sells, lends, or otherwise distributes a class of Goods. In the prototypical case, the Distributor is a retailer who generally keeps some type of Goods on site for the purpose of selling it to a buyer. Extensions include lending Goods (e.g., libraries, movie rental outlets), organization-internal distribution (as in a hospital), or other non-commercial distribution centers. The Goods are constrained to be a type of item (e.g., canned goods, antique dressers) rather than a particular or unique item (e.g., Smith's last self-portrait, that guitar I saw here last week). Note that a Distributor may carry some particular goods, but may not have it on hand at that exact moment.
The Distributor maintains a store of Goods for the purpose of selling or otherwise distributing them.
The Goods are kept on hand and distributed by the Distributor.
The Time when the Distributor carries the Goods.
The Place indicates where the carrying of Goods occurs.

Any description of the storing of goods which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of a Distributor that also affect the action (deliberately, carefully).
This FE indicates the length of time that the Distributor carries the Goods.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.
The words in this frame involve an Undesirable_Event which affects the Undergoer negatively. No agent need be involved.
The entity that experiences the Undesirable_Event.
This FE identifies the Degree to which event occurs.
This FE indicates the Circumstances under which a warning applies. (Proper only to betide.)

A Cognizer construes an Item as belonging to a certain Category. In this process, the Cognizer may either passively perceive the Item and note that it fits the Criteria for a Category, or, alternatively, actively examine the Item for certain Criteria that define a Category (or set of Categorys). Most members of the frame can also describe a resulting cognitive state of the Cognizer with respect to the Item and Category which no longer requires the current perception or consideration of the Item. A few LUs (e.g. peg.v, pigeonhole.v) do not readily allow stative interpretation, and a few LUs (e.g. deem.v, regard.v) only allow stative interpretation. You 've already stereotyped me as a bimbo, have n't you?
This is the person who performs an act of categorization. Typically, this frame element is expressed as an External Argument.
This is the entity which is construed or treated by the Cognizer as being an instance of a particular Category. Typically, the Item is expressed as an Object.
This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Item is considered an instance. Typically, it is expressed in a prepositional phrase headed by as or under.

This frame element expresses properties of the Item which is used as a basis for categorization. Criteria are the general dimensions along which Items can potentially differ from one another and hence, fall into different Categorys. For example, a paint sample can be classified by color or by finish (matte or gloss); if they are classified by color, one can be classified as orange and another as red. The Criteria FE is typically expressed as a PP headed by by, or as a complex PP of the form on the basis of...:
An act whereby the Cognizer categorizes.
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization was made.
The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the categorization holds.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
The reason for which the Cognizer categorizes the Item in the given way.

A Cause causes an Effect. Alternatively, an Actor, a participant of a (implicit) Cause, may stand in for the Cause. Those frames that inherit the Causation frame have as their background the idea that some event is responsible for the occurrence of another event (or state). In the inheriting frame, typically an FE like Agent or Causer is proposed in the place of the Actor, but in the daughter frames, as in this frame, the Actor is semantically dependent on the idea of a Cause (an event or state-of-affairs) that the Actor is a participant in. He made me angry. If such a small earthquake causes problems, just imagine a big one! The strange mutations of the rumor mill in the end led to it being said that he was actually a woman. You 've made it impossible to continue! The ending left me feeling kinda empty.
A force, process, or event that produces an effect.
Agents in a joint or reciprocal action (e.g. exchange)
A positive or negative evaluation of the Phenomenon.
The Reason for which an event occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
An entity which participates in a Cause, perhaps volitionally and perhaps not.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (the same way) and descriptions pertaining to the Actor's influence on the character of the event (eagerly, quietly).
The natural reason for which the Causation occurs.
An action through which the Actor or Cause accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
How often the action denoted by the target occurs.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
A Causation event (the Cause) causes a Result event (the Effect).
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The Effect is the event which results from the Cause.
An Agent or Cause affects a Body_part of an Experiencer so that the quality of the Experiencer's perceptual experience of the Body_part is qualitatively changed.
The Agent is the person causing a bodily experience in the Experiencer.
The Experiencer is the being or entity whose experience changes.
Result identifies the result of the Agent's action.
Degree is the degree to which the Experiencer's bodily experience is affected.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
Place identifies the place where the bodily experience is caused.
Time identifies the time when the experience-causing event occurs.
>The Body_part identifies the location on the Experiencer's body where the bodily experience takes place.
This FE is any object manipulated by the Agent to cause the experience.
Purpose identifies the state-of-affairs that an Agent hopes to bring about by causing an experience in the Experiencer.
Depictive identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action or the affected entity.
This FE identifies the event within which the bodily experience is caused.
A fact or action somehow related to the Experiencer that the Agent responds to by causing an experience in the Experiencer.
Iterations refers to the number of times the Agent or Cause causes an experience.
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that affects the Experiencer's Body_part.
The Subregion_bodypart defines the precise location on the Body_part in which the experience occurs.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the causal event and any of its participants.
How often the Cause_bodily_experience event occurs.
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cause_bodily_experience event to its end.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
This FE indicates that the Cause_bodily_experience event is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the Cause_bodily_experience event) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
A description presenting a separate aspect of the experience-causing event.
The length of time from when the Cause_bodily_experience event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

An Agent or Cause causes an Entity to change, either in its category membership or in terms of the value of an Attribute. In the former case, an Initial_category and a Final_category may be expressed, in the latter case an Initial_value and a Final_value can be specified. Our storylines follows the saga outlined by the Ultima Series, but we have modified it in order to make our writing more cohesive. I don't think you can turn that rabbit into a hat. How can a guy that changed his name from Bob Craft to Jack Ass declare anyone defamed his character? At this juncture, a new development changed the political situation on the island. She had at some time earlier completely changed her clothing and appearance and now stood in front of me dressed like a garden gnome. Hence, when (Hg 0 ) is converted to Hg 2+ , it can be rapidly taken up in rain water, snow, or adsorbed onto small particles Hence, when (Hg 0 ) is converted to Hg 2+ , it can be rapidly taken up in rain water, snow, or adsorbed onto small particles
The sentient entity that effects a change in the Entity.
The category of which the Entity is a member before the Agent causes a change.
The category that the Entity belongs to after it has undergone the change.
The value that the Attribute assumes as a result of the change that the Entity is caused to undergo.
The value that the Attribute has before the change takes place.
The time at which the change of the Entity is caused.
The extent to which the initial and final categories or values differ from each other.

Any description of the event causing the change of the Entity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in bringing about the change in the Entity.
A characteristic of the Entity for which a value can be assigned or determined by calculation, measurement , or observation.
The abstract or concrete thing or situation that the Agent causes to change.
An event that causes a change in the Entity.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by effecting a change in the Entity.
An intentional action performed by the Agent (or event resulting from the Cause) that produces a change in the Entity.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The location where the change of the Entity is caused.

Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
The particular role that the Agent plays in the Cause_change event.
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.
The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.
This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

In this frame an Agent or Cause changes the consistency of an Undergoer from its Initial_state to a Result. This may take place under certain Circumstances for a Purpose or Reason in a certain Manner. A Change_agent can also be used. Note that this frame contrasts with Cause_change_of_phase in that this frame describes causation of a change in an Undergoer within a particular phase. Donna thinned the soup with chicken broth. The high temperatures curdled the milk.
This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the consistency change occurs.
Degree to which the Undergoer changes consistency.
This is the original state of the Undergoer.
The Manner in which the Undergoer's consistency is changed.
Where the the Undergoer changes consistency.
This FE identifies theReason for which the Undergoer's consistency is changed.
Result is the result of the change of consistency.
The Speed at which the change of consistency occurs.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Undergoer is the entity that undergoes a change.
The Agent causes the change of consistency in the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent changes the consistency of the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent changes the consistency of the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent changes the consistency of the Undergoer.
The Cause is the non-Agent which brings about the change in the Undergoer.
The Change_agent is the substance used to change the consistency of the Undergoer.
This FE marks expressions that indicate a Container in which the Undergoer is changing consistency.
The HotCold_source is the source of the heat or coolness.

A Cause or Agent causes an Undergoer to undergo a change of phase. The Result of the change may be given, along with the Initial_state and the Circumstances under which the change can occur. Note that this frame contrasts with Cause_change_of_consistency in that this frame describes causation of a change of an Undergoer between different phases (i.e. solid to liquid or frozen to "unfrozen"). Bob melted the butter. Sally defrosted the chicken to eat for dinner.
The Agent causes the Undergoer to change phase.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent intentionally affects the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent intentionally affects the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent intentionally affects the Undergoer
The Undergoer undergoes a change of phase brought about by the Agent.
This FE identifies the place where change of phase occurs.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent affects the Undergoer,
This FE identifies the Time at which the change of phase occurs.
This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the phase change occurs
Degree to which the Agent changes the phase of the Undergoer
This is the original state of the Undergoer.
Result is the result of the change of phase.
The Speed at which the change of phase occurs.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
The Cause is the non-Agent which brings about the change in the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Container that holds the Undergoer whose phase is being changed .
The length of time for which the Agent changes the phase of the Undergoer.
The Depictive describes the state of the Agent or Undergoer at the time of phase change.
The Medium is the substance which surrounds the Undergoer and facilitates its phase change.
The Hot/Cold_source is the source of the heat or cool.

This frame consists of words that indicate that an Agent or a Cause affects the position of an Item on some scale (the Attribute) to change it from an initial value (Value_1) to an end value (Value_2). The direction of the change (Path) can be encoded as well as the magnitude of the change (Difference). The rate of change of the value (Speed) can optionally be indicated as well as a second scale (Co_Variable), which the values are correlated with.
The person who causes an entity (Item) to change its positon on a scale with respect to some property (Variable).
The distance between the orginial value (Value-1) and the final value (Value-2) of the entity on the scale (Variable).
The scale along which the Item ranges in value.
The initial value of the entity (Item) along the scale.
The final position on the scale that the entity (Item) assumes.
The Co-Variable is the scale that the (dependent ) Variable is measured against.
Any expression that says something about the movement of the entity (Item) along the scale between its initial (Value-1) and its final position (Value-2).
The rate at which the entity's positon on the scale changes.
The entity whose position along a scale is being changed.
An act performed by the Agent that brings about the change in the position of the Item on the scale.
The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
The force that causes the change.

Any description of the Agent changing the value of an Attribute which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The location where the Agent changes the value of an Attribute.
An Agent causes a Patient to be more strong, often resulting in something that is more secure and safe.
The Patient is the entity that is being made stronger.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
The resultant state of the action.
An act performed by anAgent that enables them to act upon the Patient.

Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The time at which the Agent makes the Patient stronger.
The location at which the Agent fortifies the Patient.
An event which causes the Patient to become stronger.
This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
The Circumstances of the world at the time of the event (which do not bear directly on the event itself).
An Agent acts to cause a Experiencer to feel a certain emotion. I was so offended by her behaviour towards me. It does not matter if the cartoon is insulting to men.
The Agent is the person who's action's cause an emotion in the Experiencer.
The Experiencer feels an emotion as caused by the Agent.
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
The tool used by the Agent to cause an emotion in the Experiencer.
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
An act performed by anAgent that enables them to act upon the Experiencer.
In what way the Agent causes an emotion in the Experiencer.
This FE describes the event as a whole, often as a VPing.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.
This FE describes the reason for the state of affairs described by the target.
For how long instances of an Agent causing the Patient an emotion has repeatedly occured.
When the Agent causes emotion in the Experiencer.

This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.
The Event is the occasion or happening that evokes emotions in the Experiencer. This Event occurs as the direct result of a sentient being's actions.
Type designates the kind of emotion that the Agent causes the Experiencer to have.
Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Agent causes the Experiencer to feel an emotion.

An Agent or non-human Cause causes an Item to change its physical size. The Size_change of an Item may be explicitly indicated or characterized in terms of Initial_size and/or Result_size. In the default case, expansion is along all dimensions, but sometimes the Dimension of expansion is incorporated or made explicit. If the design crashes too often, then try lengthening the wings by a few centimeters, to perhaps 30cm total. CNI INI As the juice churned with natural process of changing into wine, the gas it created would expand the balloon, and when the balloon eventually deflated, it was ready to drink.
With some words in this frame, an Agent who causes the change in size of the Item may be present. The Agent typically occurs as the External Argument of a verb.
The Item is frequently the External Argument of verbs or the NP Object if an Agent is expressed.
Initial_size is rarely expressed without Result_size also being explicit. Initial_size generally occurs in a PP-from Complement.
Result_size is typically expressed in a PP Complement headed by to.
Size_change identifies the amount by which the size of an Item changes.
Change of size may be limited to or described in terms of a single Dimension.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent brings about the expansion of the Item.
This FE identifies the Manner of performing an action.
The feature that the size of the Item is varied in step with.
This FE identifies the Group in which an Item changes size.
Rate identifies the rate of change of the value.
The Cause is a non-human entity which brings about the change in size.
The Elapsed_time is the amonut of time in which the change occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent causes the Item to expand.
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent cause the expansion of the Item.
This FE identifies the Reason for which the Agent cause the expansion of the Item.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent causes the expansion of the Item.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent causes the expansion of the Item.
An Agent or a Cause causes a Fluid to move from a Source to a Goal along a Path or within an Area.
The animate protagonist who causes the Fluid to move.
An event or force that causes the Fluid to move.
The entity that changes location and moves in a fluidic way. It is not necessarily in a liquid state but is construed that way.
The location that the Fluid occupies initially.
Goal is the location the Fluid ends up in as a result of the motion
The trajectory along which the Fluid moves, exclusive of the Source and Goal.
The setting in which the Fluid's movement takes place along an unspecified Path.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). With agentive uses, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The Time when the fluidic motion event is caused.
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in causing the Fluid to move.
A state of the Fluid that results from the motion event.
The location where the motion takes place.
The entity manipulated by the Agent which causes the Fluid to move.
An action of the Agent which brings about the motion of the Fluid.
The state-of-affairs that the Agent is attempting to bring about by causing motion.
The distance travelled by the Fluid.

The words in this frame describe situations in which an Agent or a Cause injures a Victim. The Body_part of the Victim which is most directly affected may also be mentioned in the place of the Victim. In such cases, the Victim is often indicated as a genitive modifier of the Body_part, in which case the Victim FE is indicated on a second FE layer.
Agent is the person causing the Victim's injury.
The Victim is the being or entity that is injured. If the Victim is included in the phrase indicating Body_part, the Victim FE is tagged on a second FE layer (see 3rd example).
Result identifies the result of the Agent's action.
Degree is the degree to which the Agent causes harm to the Victim.
The Manner in which the Agent acts upon the Victim.
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
Place identifies the place where the harm causing event occurs.
Time identifies the time when the harm-causing event occurs.
The Body_part identifies the location on the body where the bodily injury takes place.
This FE is any object used to cause the injury.
Purpose identifies the purpose for which a harm-causing action is carried out.
Depictive identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
This FE identifies the event in which the harm is caused.
A fact or action somehow related to the Victim that the Agent responds to by causing harm to the Victim.
Iterations refers to the number of times the Agent causes harm to the Victim.
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that inflicts harm on the Victim
The Subregion_bodypart defines the precise location on the Body_part which is harmed.
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Cause_harm event and any of its participants.
How often the Cause_harm event occurs.
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cause_harm event to its end.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
This FE indicates that the Cause_harm event is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the Cause_harm event) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.
A description of the harm event which significantly displays a different aspect.
The length of time from when the Cause_harm event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

An Agent causes an Impactor to make sudden, forcible contact with an Impactee, or manipulates two (or more) Impactors so that they make mutual forcible contact. He slammed his fist down on the table and bellowed something unintelligible.
The Force is the amount of force in the course of the impact.
The Impactee is the entity which is hit by the Impactor.
The Impactor is the entity that hits the Impactee because of the Agent's efforts.
The Impactors are the multiple entities that collide.
The FE Manner identifies the manner in which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.
This FE identifies the Result of the impact.
This FE indicates the Speed of the Impactor (or Impactors at impact.
Subregion identifies the part of the larger whole which was hit.
This FE identifies the Time when the impact occurs.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects an Impactee.
The FE Means identifies the means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.
The FE Purpose identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects the Impactee.
This FE identifies the Period_of_iterations during which the Agent repeatedly causes impacts.
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes an Impactor to make sudden, forcible contact with an Impactee.

An Agent causes a Theme to undergo directed motion. The motion may be described with respect to a Source, Path and/or Goal. In contrast with Placing, the Goal of motion is not emphasized. For many of these words (cast.v, throw.v, chuck.v, etc.), the Agent has control of the Theme only at the Source of motion, and does not experience overall motion. For others (e.g. drag.v, push.v, shove.v, etc.) the Agent has control of the Theme throughout the motion; for these words, the Theme is resistant to motion due to some friction with the surface along which they move. (They thus differ from the words of the Carrying frame in that they are supported by this surface, rather than a Carrier.) This frame contrasts with the following frames which talk about an Agent changing a Theme's position with respect to a landmark (either Source or Goal): In Placing, the figure (Theme) is profiled as the object, and ends up on the ground (Goal). Joyce placed the flowers onto the bed. In Filling, the ground (Goal) is profiled as the object, and the figure (Theme) ends up on the ground (Goal). John filled the box with old toys. In Removing, the figure (Theme) is profiled, and is removed from the ground (Source). Jennifer removed the flowers from the bed. In Emptying, the ground (Source) is profiled and the figure (Theme) is removed from it. Jason emptied the box of the old toys .
The the Agent is the one whose action causes the motion of a Theme. The Agent is generally realized as the External Argument.
The FE Theme is generally an NP Object.
The FESource is the starting point of motion.
The FE Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal.
The FE Goal is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion.
The FE Distance is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme.

The FE Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element.
The state of a participant during the action
The FE Means indicates the action that is taken that results in the motion of the Theme

The FE Manner is any expression which describes a property of the motion of the Theme which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Subregion identifies the part of the Theme that makes contact with the resulting location. When Subregion is expressed, there usually is no Goal expressed.
Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes the Theme to be set in motion.
An entity saliently involved in the transmission of force from an Agent to a Theme. It may be the Agent's bodypart, or some kind of device.
The Place is the general area that provides a setting for a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal).
The time at which the motion of the Theme occurs.
A resultant state that the Theme is in at the end of its motion.
The Agent's manipulation of the Theme may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Theme, a Handle. The Handle is usually expressed as a PP
A previous state that the Theme was in before the beginning of its motion.
This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

An Agent (or inanimate Cause) affects a Set so that the number of entities that make up the Set changes from an Initial_number to a Final_number. Alternatively, the situation can be described in terms of an Initial_state and a Final_state. In some cases the Attribute (i.e., number) or Difference in number may be mentioned. More and more resources have been devoted to halting rogue nation's proliferation of controlled nuclear technology.
The person who causes the Set to increase in number.
The distance between the orginal value (Initial_number) and the final value (Final_number) of the Set.
The scale along which the Set ranges in, i.e., number.
The initial number of entities in the Set.
The final number of entities in the Set.
The Co-Variable is the scale that the amount of the Set is measured against.
Any expression that says something about the movement of the entity (Set) along the scale between its Initial_number and its Final_number.
The rate at which the entity's positon on the scale changes.
The entity whose amount is being changed.
An act performed by the Agent that brings about the change in the number of the Set.
The purpose for which the proliferating of the number of a Set is performed.
The force that causes the change.

Any description of the Agent changing the number of the Set which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The location where the Agent changes the number of the Set.
The state of the Set before it is affected by an outside Agent or Cause.
The state of the Set after it is affected by an outside Agent or Cause.

In this frame, an Agent changes the temperature of an Item. A Temperature_goal can specify the desired temperature. A Temperature_change can also be indicated. The Temperature_start indicates the initial temperature. Margaret Anne chilled the salad to 30 degrees. Heat the water 30 degrees.
The Agent performs the intentional act which changes the temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
The Item undergoes the temperature change.
The Temperature_goal is the temperature to which the Agent is heating or cooling the Item.
The Temperature_change is the amount of difference between the intial and goal temperatures.
Temperature_start is the initial temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
Result is the resultant state of the Agent changing the temperature of the Item.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that changes the temperature. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The length of time for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
This FE identifies the Container that holds the Item whose temperature is being changed.
This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Item.
The Hot_Cold_source is the source of the heat or coolness.
This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the temperature change occurs.
The degree to which the Item approaches (an implicit) Temperature_goal, which is often construed to be the ambient temperature.

These words refer to an Agent joining Parts to form a Whole. (The Parts may also be encoded as Part_1 and Part_2.) There is a symmetrical relationship between the components that undergo the process, and afterwards the Parts are consumed and are no longer distinct entities that are easily discernable or separable in the Whole. Chuck merged the corpora. Chuck merged the corpora into a database. Chuck merged the BNC with the AP Corpus into a database. The two forces merged into a single, undifferentiated mass of murderous mayhem.(Sense 2) Melt the butter, then blend it with the room temperature milk. CNI
In causative uses of these verbs there is an Agent responsible for amalgamating the Parts. The Agent is generally the External Argument (or the object of a PP-by in passives).
This FE identifies Whole as the entity resulting from combination of Parts. When overtly expressed, it is usually a PP Complement (often headed by into).
This FE identifies the Parts entities being combined, and is often expressed in a single plural NP, usually the direct object of a verb.
This FE identifies the first of two Parts mentioned. It is most often the NP-Object of a verb.
This FE identifies the second of two Parts mentioned. It is usually a PP Complement.
This FE identifies the Manner in which the amalgamating occurs.
This FE identifies the thoroughness of the mixing job, i.e. to what degree the resulting Whole is undifferentiated.
This FE identifies the Means by which the amalgamating occurs.
This FE is used for indicating the Result of amalgamating.
The state of the Parts during the amalgamation. Often it refers to the proportion of the Parts to one another.
The state of affairs that the Agent seeks to bring about by the Amalgamation.
The location that the event occurs.
The time at which the amalgamation occurs.

An Agent causes a Dryee (either a surface or an entire entity, inside and out) to become dry. This should not include examples like "drying tears" or "drying spills" as these are in the Removing frame. Michael dried the clothes. Abby dried out the room with a dehumidifier.
The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the Dryee to become dry.
The Dryee is the entity which has the water removed from it.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
This FE identifies theManner in which an the Agent dries the Dryee.
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which Agent intentionally affects the Dryee and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of dryness. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
This FE identifies the length of Time that the drying takes.
This FE identifies the Temperature at which heat is applied to the Dryee.
The degree to which the Dryee ends up dry.

An Agent or Causemakes a New_member part of Group. The Group may be represented by an individual Existing_member if it implies the existence of a set of members. I added a new rock to my collection. He decided he needed to add a red tie to the blue tie in his closet.
The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the New_member to become part of the Group.
Something that is already a member of the Group and represents the Group as a whole.
An item that becomes a part of the Group.
The Group is anything that can be conceptualized as a complex collection of parts or ingredients, including through metonymy like containers or locations, which New_members can join.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that is responsible for causing a New_member to enter a Group.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the inclusion of a New_member.
This FE identifies when the inclusion of the New_member to the Group occurs.
The manner in which the Agent acts.
This FE identifies what the Agent hopes to accomplish by including a New_member to a Group.
The location in which a New_member is entered into a pre-existing Group.
An Agent or Cause makes a Patient sharper or duller. An Instrument or Means may be mentioned. John is in the basement sharpening his axe.
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the sharpening (or dulling) action.
The Agent causes the Patient to become more or less sharp.
An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an Patient, causing it to change in sharpness.
This FE identifies the place where the Agent sharpens the Patient.
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent sharpens the Patient.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent sharpens Patient.
The Patient is the entity that is sharpened.
The manner in which the Agent changes the sharpness of the Patient.
The state of affairs that the Agent is responding to by executing the sharpening act.
The extent to which the Patient's sharpness is affected by the Agent.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of sharpness. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
The resulting configuration of the Patient.

An Agent causes an Undergoer to be wet with a Liquid. In this frame, the Liquid can be a liquid or gas. Undergoers are porous objects, but not hollow (like containers). Jo soaked the dog with water. Ellen wet the sponge with water.
The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the Undergoer to become wet.
The Liquid is a fluid or gas that permeates or covers the Undergoer. It most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with.
The Undergoer takes up the Liquid through its pores or has the Liquid covering its surface.
This FE identifies the Manner or way in which the Agent wets the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Means by which an the Agent wets the Undergoer
This FE identifies the Place where the Agent wets the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent wets the Undergoer and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent wets the Undergoer.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally wets the Undergoer.
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of wetness.
Degree to which the Agent wets the Undergoer.
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
This FE describes the reason for the state of the Cause_to_be_wet event.
An Agent causes a Process or State to continue. The goaltenders kept the game going with terrific saves.
The individual who causes the Process to continue or the State to be maintained.
A Process that is maintained by the Agent.
The State that the Agent maintains.
The length of time for which the Agent maintain the State or Process.
The event by which an Agent or Cause maintains the State or Process.
An event that causes the Process or State to be maintained.
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by maintaining the State or Process.
An entity directed by the Agent that maintain the State or Process.
The time at which the Process continues.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
The location at which the Process continues.
An Agent or Cause causes a Process or State to end. Bush may lift sanctions on his own, despite opposition.
Name of the event which is brought to an end.
An action of the Agent that causes the Process to end.
Where the Process or State is caused to end.
The Reason for which the event is ended.
The Time when the event is ended.
The Degree to which the Process is brought to an end.
Depictive phrase describing the actor of the event that causes the Process to end.
The Manner of causing the Process to end.
The individual who causes the Process or State to end.
An event that causes the Process to be ended.
A State which is ended by the Agent or Cause.

An Agent intentionally seeks to bring about an internal mental or emotional state in the Experiencer. This frame in closely related to Experiencer_obj. Samantha terrorized the children into screaming.
This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent intentionally tries to bring about an internal mental or emotional state.
The Agent is an External Argument of the target word and purposefully arouses an emotional state.
The Experiencer is the person the Agent causes to have a particular emotional state.
This Frame Element is for expressions that elaborate the manner in which the Agent affects the Experiencer.
What the Agent intends to make the Experiencer do by causing a certain experience and the Experiencer actually does.
This FE identifies the Time when the Agent affects the Experiencer.
This FE identifies the Place where theAgent affects the Experiencer
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent brings about the emotional state.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent brings about the emotional state in the Experiencer.
Degree to which the Experiencer ends up feeling an emotion.

An Agent suddenly and often violently separates the Whole_patient into two or more smaller Pieces, resulting in the Whole_patient no longer existing as such. Several lexical items are marked with the semantic type Negative, which indicates that the fragmentation is necessarily judged as injurious to the original Whole_patient. Compare this frame with Damaging, Render_non-functional, and Removing. He ripped up the letter faster than you can say "Jack Robbins". INI Don't go in there or you 'll be torn to bits! CNI She shattered the vase with a casual backhand blow to make it look like there had been a struggle. INI Tear into 6" strips, each about one inch wide, then bake at 400. CNI CNI
The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the Whole_patient being broken into Pieces.
An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with a Whole_patient to accomplish its fracture.

Any description of the fracturing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the breakage.
The entity which is destroyed by the Agent and that ends up broken into Pieces.
This FE identifies the place where the Agent breaks the Whole_patient into pieces.
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent causes the break-up of the Whole_patient.
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.
This FE identifies the time when the Agent breaks up the Whole_patient.
The fragments of the Whole_patient that result from the Agent's action.
The degree to which the fracturing is completed.
The part of the Whole_patient which is directly affected by the breakage.
This FE identifies the Result of an event.
The Resistant_surface is the surface against which a Agent presses the Whole_patient.
An event which leads to the fragmentation of the Whole_patient.
An Agent manipulates a Sound_maker or a Cause causes the Sound_maker to emit a sound. The monks would ring the bell until sundown.
The individual that manipulates a Sound_maker so that it makes Noise.
The entity that produces the Noise, as a result of the action of the Agent.
The Subregion is the sublocation of the Sound_maker from which the sound is emitting.
The location from which the noise emanates toward an (implicit) perceiver.
The state of one of the primary participants (either Agent or Sound_maker) during the course of the sound-making event.

Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
An action directly due to the Agent or Cause that results in the Sound_maker emitting noise..
The inanimate force of nature that causes the Sound_maker to produce noise.
The change or state of affairs preceding the event, deemed to have caused the event.
The state-of-affairs or action that the Agent wishes to bring about by performing the action.
The time at which the noise is produced.
The location at which the sound is produced.
The number of times the Sound_maker makes noise per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.
Used for expressions that indicate the number of times Sound_maker makes noise.
An Agent works on a Project so that it reaches a more advanced and desirable state.
The object or idea that undergoes change due to the efforts of the Agent.
The former state of the Project.
The state of the Project following an advance.
The time at which the progress occurs.
The rate at which the change happens.
A description of the progress, generally a description comparing events (the same way); in addition, it may describe characteristics and states of the Agent that also affect the development.
The period over which the Agent develops the Project.
The amount of advancement that the Project has attained.
The individual that brings about the development of the Project.
The location at which the the Project progresses.
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent progresses the Project.
The action of the Agent which enables the advancement.

An Agent causes a Theme to move with respect to a certain Fixed_location, generally with a certain Periodicity, without undergoing unbounded translational motion or significant alteration of configuration/shape. Paul shook the remote control frantically.
Theme identifies the object involved in motion.
This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.
The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.
This FE identifies the Reason for which an event occurs.
This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.
The Means is the way in which the motion in place is instigated.
The number of times the Theme returns to a state in a given duration.
The point or set of points that define the limits of motion for the Theme. For spinning motions, it is the axis, for vibrating it is a boundary, for swinging it is a point.
The Agent performs the intentional act.
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.
Angle identifies the amount that the Theme turns.
The Agent's manipulation of an Theme may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Theme, a Locus. This FE is usually expressed as a PP Complement.
This FE identifies the part of the Agent's body being used to manipulate the Theme.
Cause identifies the non-agentive force that causes the motion in place.
This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, that express the Direction of the swinging, vibrating or rotating.
This FE identifies the Result of an event.

An Agent, Actor, Entity, or Medium causes a Phenomenon to be perceived by a Perceiver. With an Actor, Entity, or Medium, the Perceiver is usually unspecified. Aileen showed Rob the book. He exhibited great interest in the project. The second scene depicts Dad holding the ball for a place kick. The economy is showing signs of growth. NB: This may change in the future, but as of now this frame subsumes three closely-related cause/perceiver alternations: a.) perception of a specific Perceiver caused by an Agent, b.) perception of some implicit audience caused, possibly unintentionally, by an Actor, and c.) perception of some implicit audience caused by a Medium or Entity. Perhaps this frame is too broad - the different subject FEs seem to all indicate different ways of "showing."
The Agent intentionally creates a situation in which the Perceiver observes or experiences the Phenomenon.
The Phenomenon is an entity or idea that is perceived by the Perceiver.
The Perceiver is made to have a perceptual experience by the Agent.
The instrument or method by which the Perceiver was shown the Phenomenon.
A description of the way in which the Agent presents the Phenomenon.
Frequency describes how often the Agent presents the Phenomenon.
The location where the Agent causes the perception of the Perceiver.
The purpose of the Agent in creating the perception of the Perceiver.
An Actor is a sentient being who is exhibiting, possibly uninintentionally, some Phenomenon.
An object that has some association with a Phenomenon.
The Medium through which a Phenomenon is expressed.
A Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the Actor or Agent.
